key_insight: An uncertainty-aware framework translates predicted patient deterioration risk into ICU staffing plans that balance staffing costs against severe shortage exposure.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support ICU workforce planning while accounting for hiring delays and inflexible shifts, without changing the underlying prediction model.
method: Aggregate patient risk predictions while explicitly modeling dynamic predictive uncertainty.
Use Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to quantify extreme shortage exposure.
Embed risk-calibrated demand signals in hourly rolling-horizon staffing decisions.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on realistic MIMIC-IV trajectories showed a favorable cost–shortage trade-off versus deterministic and reactive baselines, with Pareto analysis and calibration-drift stress testing.
watch_item: The abstract reports trajectory-based evaluation rather than prospective deployment, so real-world staffing feasibility and patient-care effects remain unestablished.
paper_title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing
